text:
michael: Quick follow-up from the INC-2026 postmortem — want to lock down remediation owners, timelines, and exact runbook edits for the recurring KV cache eviction pattern we saw. Putting a single thread together so we don't scatter action items.

elena: Thanks — yes. Main asks: 1) update triage checklist with the new `cache-evict` indicators, 2) add explicit escalation path if canary recovery fails, 3) create a shortplay for urgent cache rollback. Who wants to own each? :clipboard:

jess: I can own the runbook edits (triage checklist + commands). Planning a PR with diffs and a sample runbook snippet by EOW (Fri).

adele: I'll own the escalation path and PagerDuty flow. We need to decide the 3-tier escalation and fallback model (model-variant fallback -> region failover -> capacity fallback). Targeting next Wed for final doc.

paul: I'll take monitoring/alerting: add an aggregated alert (KV_EVICT_RATE > 0.5% over 5min) and a dashboard tile. Will also add an automated correlation to recent deploys so triage starts with deploy-checks.

michael: Perfect. For runbook commands, Jess — can you include the minimal set we used during the incident? Suggest including the `inspect-kv` and `force-evict` quick commands we ran.

jess: Yep — draft snippet below for the triage section:```bash
# check recent evictions in the inference shard
rictl logs svc/inference --since 15m | jq 'select(.event=="kv_evict")' | tail -n 50
# check kv cache hit ratio
redwood-metrics query 'kv_cache_hit_ratio{shard="inference"}' --last 5m
# quick eviction (manual)
rictl exec svc/inference --force-kv-evict --shard inference
```

elena: Love the concise commands. Add a one-liner that explains when to run `--force-kv-evict` vs waiting for automated backoff.

jess: Will do. Also adding the optional safety check: `--dry-run` and `--confirm` flags in the examples.

paul: On alerts — I'll add a runbook section that links directly to the incident timeline and the postmortem doc (`https://pm.redwood/internal/inc-2026`). Good to have context in alert details.

sre-bot: [incident-bot] Postmortem created: https://pm.redwood/internal/inc-2026 — team owners: jess (runbook), adele (escalation), paul (monitoring).

adele: For escalation: propose the following ladder — P1 alert -> oncall -> 15m triage -> if no recovery, notify infra-engineering lead + start canary rotate; if still failing after 30m, trigger region fallback plan. I'll write the exact PD escalation entries.

michael: Sounds good. One more ask — we observed a recurring pattern linked to short bursts of long sequences from a specific customer flow. Can we add a mitigation note to the runbook: temporary tokenization/proxy limit for that flow + contact CS to throttle?

jess: Adding a 'customer-impact mitigation' subsection with exact commands to throttle a customer key and a template message for CS to send.

elena: Timeline recap: jess PR by Fri (runbook + commands), adele PD/escalation doc by Wed, paul alert + dashboard by Tue. Michael will follow up in 7 days to confirm PR merged and runbook published.

michael: I'll create a single GitHub issue that links all PRs and the postmortem, and ping owners. File created: https://git.redwood/ops/inc-2026-remediations. Owners — please add checklist items to that issue with your subtasks.

jess: Added checklist and pinned the draft runbook PR in the issue. Marking this as my WIP. :white_check_mark:

adele: Drafted PD entries and will request PD policy approval after a quick sync with security on notification content.

paul: Alert rule queued, dashboard tile created, will submit infra change request if the rule needs wide rollout.

michael: Great work. I'll re-check in on Monday to confirm progress and we can close this follow-up. If anything slips, call it out here so we can reassign. :smiley:
